title: [3.13] gh-140594: Fix an out of bounds read when feeding NUL byte to PyOS_StdioReadline() (GH-140910) (#145853)
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in PyOS_StdioReadline (myreadline.c:345) in a 100-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: libc malloc (the object never reaches a pymalloc pool)
layer_note: measured: the heap report SURVIVES PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc, so the object is not a pymalloc block. It is PyMem_RawMalloc d (myreadline.c:207,223,325,347) -- a libc block at 100 bytes, which is why the <=512 B shortcut was wrong
status: host oracle measured 2026-10-06 on the pinned ASan build; no arm has been run
